chunks: A group informed me, from Abū Muḥammad Hārūn ibn Mūsā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Saʿīd, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan. And Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdūn informed me, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zurārah, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿUmar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurārah and al-Fuḍayl, from one of the two of them, peace be upon them, who said:
The woman in nifās refrains from salat (prayer) for the days of her aqrāʾ during which she used to remain [in menstruation], then she performs ghusl and prays just as the mustaḥāḍah performs ghusl.

key_terms.أَيَّامَ أَقْرَائِهَا: the days of her usual menstrual cycle
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the ritual prayer that is temporarily left during nifās
key_terms.النُّفَسَاءُ: a woman in the state of postnatal bleeding
key_terms.الْمُسْتَحَاضَةُ: a woman experiencing istiḥāḍah whose purification procedure is referenced here

ai.seo_question: How long does a woman in nifās leave salat (prayer), and when does she perform ghusl and resume praying?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding the woman in nifās, stating that she leaves salat (prayer) for the number of days corresponding to her usual menstrual period. After that, she performs ghusl and resumes salat (prayer), following the manner of the mustaḥāḍah in purification.
